newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico mortgage debt restructuring period extended.
newsitem.headline: Mexico mortgage debt restructuring period extended.

text.p: Mexican banks have decided to extend the period to restructure mortgage debts, the National Bank and Securities Commission (CNBV) said.
Debtors may apply today for mortgage restructuring. Previously, today was to be the deadline for completing the restructuring, the CNBV said.
The extension will not affect the cost of the program, the CNBV said.
But the commission said the extension for mortgage debt does not apply to the general debt relief program known as ADE. That application deadline is today.
The government and private banks established the debt relief programs following the December 1994 peso devaluation and ensuing economic crisis that led to soaring interest rates.
The CNBV said it has renegotiated 788,074 mortgages of 893,000 eligible under the program.
